key_insight: MedCORE makes medical image diagnosis more interpretable by forcing the model to reason through clinician-defined criteria rather than jumping straight from pixels to labels.
clinical_relevance: This could improve transparency and trust in AI-assisted diagnosis by showing which morphological and textural findings support each prediction across different imaging modalities.
method: Localizes each diagnostic criterion to relevant image regions
Uses multi-scale evidence to capture both coarse structure and fine texture
Refines criteria with a graph attention network and uncertainty-calibrated weighting
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on ISIC 2018, BUSI, and IDRiD, reaching 89.2%/85.7%/96.4% (accuracy/macro-F1/AUC) on ISIC, 96.1%/95.2%/98.4% on BUSI, and 84.3%/80.2%/92.8% on IDRiD.
watch_item: Because the framework is more complex than standard classifiers, real-world use may depend on reliable criterion annotations, robust calibration, and careful validation before deployment.
paper_title: MedCORE: Criteria-Grounded Clinical Reasoning for Interpretable Medical Image Diagnosis
